bugs.title: Messageboard spec is blocked on a file that no longer exists
bugs.body: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-messageboard-design.md carries `Status: design only. Blocked on the dispatcher (harness/dispatch.ts), which does not exist yet.` The dispatcher exists and is Gleam: harness/src/harness/dispatch.gleam. The dependency named in the status line was superseded, not satisfied, so a reader cannot tell whether the spec is still blocked. Posts are in fact half-built: dispatch.gleam logs them as events and routes nothing. Filed rather than fixed because docs/ needs asking.

bugs.title: Guard events do not say which worker was denied
bugs.body: guard.gleam:386 logs every decision as event/tool/decision and nothing else. Under `run --concurrency 3` all three guards write to one runs/<id>/events.jsonl, so a Deny cannot be attributed to a worker or a node. Rules already carries `holder`, the identity it locks under, so the guard knows; it just does not log it. Auto-filing bugs from guard denials depends on this, so it is a prerequisite rather than a nice-to-have.

bugs.title: A parked attempt leaves its proof file on disk, untracked
bugs.body: Rule30/Proofs/EvolveLeftSecondDiagonal.lean was left on disk when Vesper's attempt was parked, untracked and not imported by Rule30/Proofs.lean. Filed as a question rather than a defect, because the evidence cuts both ways: Rowan reports the re-dispatch built that same file unchanged and the verifier passed it, so leaving it saved a proof rather than losing one. What is genuinely wrong is that the file's existence carries no signal — nothing distinguishes `abandoned debris` from `a correct proof whose attempt was mislabelled`. Resolve this one by deciding, not by deleting: wontfix with a reason is a good outcome here.

bugs.title: hit_ceiling treats allowed_warning as a closed window
bugs.body:
Reported by Rowan, agents/Rowan.md 2026-09-06T02:05:00Z, filed by Keel.

worker.gleam:871 `hit_ceiling` saw a rate_limit_event at 0.94 utilization against the 0.9 ceiling and treated the window as closed. The event's API status was `allowed_warning` — a warning, not a refusal. Combined with an errored turn this parked a finished attempt as `rate_limited`, and a rate-limited attempt stops the run from starting more, so one misread warning can halt a whole run.

Rowan's ruling on the fix: only an api_retry carrying `rate_limit`, or a status that is not `allowed*`, means the window is actually closed.
bugs.resolution: hit_ceiling now decodes rate_limit_info.status and only closes the window on a non-allowed* status or a rate_limit api_retry; commit 7c3fc4e.

bugs.title: posts is required by the report schema but optional in the decoder
bugs.body:
Reported by Rowan, agents/Rowan.md 2026-09-06T02:05:00Z, filed by Keel.

brief.gleam:80 lists `posts` in the report schema's `required` array; worker.gleam:60 decodes it with `decode.optional_field("posts", [], ...)`. The two disagree, and the CLI's side wins: it rejects the structured-output tool call before the Gleam decoder ever sees it. A report with no posts is the common case, so this fires often.

Cost, observed: Vesper proved evolve_left_second_diagonal in one shot 85 seconds in, omitted `posts`, and the turn became an error. The `proved` claim the parking code adjudicates first was inside the rejected tool call, so it never counted, and the attempt was parked as rate_limited (see hit-ceiling-misreads-allowed-warning). The proof was correct and had to be re-dispatched to be recorded.

Fix: drop `posts` from the schema's `required` list, or make schema and decoder agree either way.

Keel's note: this generalises. Any field in `required` that a worker may reasonably omit is this same bug. The bug board's own `bugs` field must NOT be added to `required` for exactly this reason — an empty array is the common case there too.
bugs.resolution: posts dropped from the report schema's required array, agreeing with the decoder's existing default of []; commit 7c3fc4e.
